title: RIS-Assisted Physical Layer Security in Emerging RF and Optical Wireless Communications Systems: A Comprehensive Survey
affiliation: McMaster University / Henan Polytechnic University / University of the Witwatersrand / University of Guelph / University of Ottawa / The American University in Cairo / Université Paris-Saclay
domain: RIS / Physical Layer Security / 6G / RF Communications / Optical Wireless / VLC / FSO / Machine Learning

analysis_policy.focus: Extract multi-part summary tables, dual-domain (RF+OWC) survey structure, per-section Lessons Learnt, technology taxonomy approach
analysis_policy.depth: Full paper analysis including fundamentals, RF systems, OWC systems, optimization, ML, and performance analysis

section_flow.title: Introduction
subsections: A. Related Work and Existing Surveys
section_flow.summary: Establishes 6G security challenges, positions PLS as alternative to cryptography, introduces RIS as enabler. Survey covers RF and OWC - unique dual-domain scope. Lists 6 contribution areas.

section_flow.title: PLS Fundamentals
section_flow.summary: Shannon's information-theoretic security, Wyner's wiretap channel, attack types (passive/active), 7 metrics (SR, SC, SOP, PNSC, IP, ESC, EST), PLS techniques (AN, BF, jamming).

section_flow.title: RIS: Architecture and Capabilities
subsections: B. Working Principles and Basic Architecture
section_flow.summary: RIS fundamentals, three architectures (single/fully/group connected), three reflection modes, optical RIS types (mirror array, metasurface, liquid crystal).

section_flow.title: RIS-Assisted PLS in RF Communication Systems
subsections: B. Integrating RIS with Enabling Technologies
section_flow.summary: PLS techniques (AN, BF, cooperative jamming), 11+ enabling technologies: mmWave, THz, AAV, D2D, CRN, SWIPT, MEC, satellite, ISAC, IoT, etc. Tables II.A-II.D summarize literature.

section_flow.title: RIS-Assisted PLS in OWC Systems
subsections: A. Integrating RIS With OWC Enabling Technologies
section_flow.summary: VLC, VLC-RF, FSO-RF hybrid systems. Different RIS types for optical (mirror array, metasurface). Table III summarizes OWC literature.

section_flow.title: Optimization Techniques for RIS-Assisted PLS
subsections: B. Other Secrecy Metrics for Optimization
section_flow.summary: Standard optimization problem formulation, SR maximization techniques (AO, BCD, SDR, SCA, MM, CCP), other metrics (SNR, power, EE, SOP). Tables IV-V summarize.

section_flow.title: Machine Learning Techniques for RIS-Assisted PLS
section_flow.summary: DRL (DDPG, DQN), unsupervised learning. Table VI summarizes ML-based optimization references.

section_flow.title: Performance Analysis for RIS-Assisted PLS
section_flow.summary: Performance analysis literature by metric type. Table VII summarizes references with attack type, phase shift resolution, and metrics.

section_flow.title: Open Research Challenges and Future Directions
section_flow.summary: Six challenge areas with specific future research directions including CoMP, blockchain, RSMA, AR/VR, underwater, mixed RIS/FSS.

section_flow.title: Conclusion
section_flow.summary: Synthesizes survey contributions covering PLS fundamentals, RIS architecture, RF and OWC systems, optimization, ML, and performance analysis.

rhetorical_contract.promise: Comprehensive overview of RIS-assisted physical layer security for both RF and optical wireless communications systems
rhetorical_contract.delivery_mechanism: PLS fundamentals → RIS architecture → RF systems (extensive) → OWC systems → Optimization → ML → Performance analysis → Future directions
rhetorical_contract.unique_contribution: First comprehensive survey covering RIS-PLS for BOTH RF and OWC with multi-part summary tables (II.A-D, III, IV-VII)

Summary of RIS-assisted PLS in OWC systems

figure_types.example: Fig. 8, 9 - RF and OWC enabling technologies

gap_identification: Discrete phase shifts need more attention

methodology.survey_approach: Fundamentals → Domain split (RF/OWC) → Methodology split (Optimization/ML) → Performance analysis → Future

reusable_writing_recipes.description: When surveying a large literature, divide references into multiple sub-tables (A, B, C, D) with consistent column structure spanning multiple pages
structure: Define consistent columns: Technology, System Model, CSI, Channel, RIS Type, PLS Technique, Eve(s), Metric(s)
Split into parts A, B, C, D based on technology categories or alphabetical order
Use 'TABLE II.A', 'TABLE II.B' numbering scheme
Each part maintains identical column headers
Span multiple pages if needed with '(CONTINUED)' suffix
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Tables II.A-D cover 100+ RIS-PLS RF references with 10 columns each
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Comprehensive coverage without overwhelming single table; enables systematic comparison; facilitates reader lookup by technology

reusable_writing_recipes.description: When covering overlapping but distinct technology domains, dedicate separate major sections with parallel internal structure
structure: Section A: Domain 1 (e.g., RF systems) with full subsection tree
Section B: Domain 2 (e.g., OWC systems) with parallel subsection tree
Both sections end with 'Lessons Learnt' subsection
Separate summary tables for each domain (Table II vs Table III)
Cross-references between domains where applicable
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section IV covers RF (8+ pages), Section V covers OWC (3+ pages) with distinct Tables II and III
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Allows deep dive into each domain while maintaining survey coherence; readers can focus on their domain of interest
reusable_writing_recipes.complexity: Medium - requires expertise in both domains

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Organize technology coverage with numbered subsection per enabling technology following consistent template
structure: Number each technology: 1) mmWave, 2) THz, 3) AAV, etc.
Each subsection: Brief intro → Integration rationale → Key references → Security benefits
Use italic technology names as headers
Maintain consistent paragraph structure across technologies
Group related technologies when natural (e.g., WPT/SWIPT together)
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section IV.B lists 11 numbered 'RIS-Assisted Secure X Communications' subsections
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Systematic coverage; easy navigation; demonstrates comprehensive scope; enables technology-specific lookup

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Conclude each major section with a dedicated 'Lessons Learnt' subsection containing synthesized bullet points
structure: Header: 'C. Lessons Learnt' (or similar letter based on section structure)
Opening: 'This section/subsection has investigated... Here are the key takeaways:'
Bullet points (4-6 typical) each covering one insight theme
Each bullet: Observation → Implication → Future direction (optional)
Bullets synthesize reading, not just summarize topics
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Sections IV.C, V.B, VI.C, VII.C, VIII.D all follow this pattern
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Provides synthesis at each milestone; highlights key insights; guides future research; aids reader comprehension
reusable_writing_recipes.complexity: Medium - requires synthesis beyond mere coverage

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Define each secrecy metric with formal mathematical expression and contextual explanation
structure: Numbered subsection per metric: '1) Secrecy Rate:', '2) Secrecy Capacity:' etc.
Opening explanation of what the metric measures
Mathematical definition with equation number
Explanation of terms and significance
Brief mention of when/why this metric is used
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section II.C defines 7 metrics (SR, SC, SOP, PNSC, IP, ESC, EST) with equations (2)-(8)
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Establishes rigorous foundations; enables reader self-sufficiency; creates reference section for rest of paper

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Structure open challenges section with dedicated subsection per emerging technology/challenge area
structure: Each subsection: A, B, C, D, E, F for different challenge areas
Subsection title indicates technology/challenge domain
Content: Current gap → Why it matters → Specific research directions
Include both incremental and transformative directions
Final subsection for 'Other Emerging Technologies' catch-all
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section IX has 6 subsections: Optimization, ML, Multiband, Movable Antenna, Generalized Fading, Other Technologies
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Actionable future work; inspires follow-on research; demonstrates author's vision for field evolution

key_concepts.pls_rationale: PLS avoids key distribution latency, works with resource-constrained devices, exploits channel randomness
key_concepts.ris_advantage: Proactively reconfigures propagation environment, low power, low cost, can direct signal to legitimate users while degrading eavesdropper
key_concepts.dual_domain_importance: 6G uses both RF (mmWave/THz) and OWC (VLC/FSO) for bandwidth needs; both have security vulnerabilities
key_concepts.integration_benefit: RIS + PLS enables information-theoretic security without encryption overhead
